messages:
maya: Heads-up: we observed a large drop in Korean->EN translation quality after int8 quant bring-up for model rwd-xl-v2. Ran FLORES-200 subset + a long-form internal news set. Full results in the artifact: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/runs/1802-kor-int8 (summary below)

li: how large is the drop? numbers?

maya: baseline fp16 BLEU=37.2, q8_0 BLEU=36.8 (ok), int8 (dynamic) BLEU=31.1, chrF++ drops from 58.4 -> 50.9. COMET also down ~0.45. This is specific to KO->EN and long inputs (>512 toks). Short sentences are fine.

sam: that's big. did you check tokenization? korean usually sensitive if we change tokenizer or added an extra pre-tokenization step.

maya: good call. I diffed tokenization between the FP and quant runtime. Found an extra normalization pass in the quant-serving path that inserts U+200B ZERO-WIDTH SPACE around punctuation for CJK to avoid merge ops. That increases token count and changes alignment for the attention cache. Example: original: "정부는 발표했다." tokenized -> ["정부", "는", "발표", "했다", "."]
quant path tokenized -> ["정부", "는", "발표", "했다", "."]

igor: wait the zero-width space is being inserted as a separate byte sequence? that will change BPE splits. can you paste exact token ids from both runs?

maya: pasted small snippet:
```
# FP16 tokens (bpe ids): 1024 4521 78 2390 13
# int8 tokens (bpe ids): 1024 68899 4521 78 2390 13
# note the extra glue token 68899 corresponds to U+200B insertion
```

sam: that extra id will shift cache indexing causing KV cache misalignment at generation time. Could explain quality drop for long context.

li: how did the zero-width insertion get introduced? config drift?

maya: yes, looks like a last-minute preprocessing optimization in the quant-serving docker (to avoid some multi-byte merge bug). It was added in commit 6a7f8 in eng-runtime and not applied to the FP path.

igor: TODOs: 1) roll back the normalization in quant path and rerun quick evals (owner: maya). 2) add a tokenization regression test across all locales for quant images (owner: li). 3) run long-form BLEU/chrF for KO/JP/zh CN with and without the fix (owner: sam). 4) add a one-off alignment check in runtime to detect new high-frequency IDs (owner: igor).

maya: starting rollback now. quick test (small batch) underway. run command used: `./scripts/run_eval.sh --model rwd-xl-v2 --quant int8 --datasets flores200:ko-en,internal-news-long-kor --maxlen 2048 --batch 2`

eval-bot: quick-run finished: BLEU int8 (post-rollback) = 36.9 (vs 31.1 pre-rollback). chrF++ = 57.1. Token delta: -3.2% (token counts closer to fp16).

li: nice, that matches hypothesis. we should still add a middleware check that rejects invisible unicode glue chars in tokenization changes.

sam: also confirm no regression on RTL languages: ran small Arabic tests — no similar invisible-char insertion there but we saw a small punctuation normalization difference for ar->en that lowered punctuation recall. file: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/rtl-checks/1802-rtl-report

maya: good call. I'll open PR to remove normalization and add cross-locale token regression tests + a failing unit test using the news-long sample.

igor: once PR is up, we should coordinate a canary rollout to dedicated pools only and monitor user-facing latency and quality SLOs for 24h. add to eng-oncall.

maya: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/eng-runtime/pull/342. includes failing test before change and golden tokens after.

li: thanks! let's also add a short doc to devex explaining how invisible separators impact BPE/quant runtimes — I've seen this bite others.

maya: will do. closing thread after we verify archived metrics in 48h. :thumbsup:
